Automated triage

Issue #47 is a small, self-contained UI enhancement with a clear outcome (guests can tell how many listings match current filters). It is independent of the pending reservation confirmation work, reuses existing search results and UI conventions, and explicitly scopes itself to a minimal change with focused tests, so an autonomous developer can execute it without needing product decisions. Priority is 'normal': it is a non-urgent UX improvement rather than a bug, security issue, or blocker; it is a good candidate for the team's normal queue as a quick win. The only ambiguities are copy phrasing (singular/plural and the zero-state label) and the exact value used for the count (derived from the same rendered results list), both resolved in the acceptance criteria in favor of the least-surprising, testable behavior: always derive the count from the currently rendered result set.

This triage note was created by an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of the user.

Acceptance criteria:
- Given a guest with stay search results, a compact result count is shown in the results area that equals the number of listed stays matching the current search query and filters.
- Changing the search query or any filter re-renders the count in the same render pass as the results, so the displayed number always matches the number of listing cards shown (no stale count, no manual refresh).
- When zero stays match, the count is phrased naturally (e.g. "0 stays" or "No matching stays") and remains visible next to the empty state rather than disappearing.
- When exactly one stay matches, the count uses singular phrasing (e.g. "1 stay"), and when more than one matches it uses plural phrasing (e.g. "12 stays").
- The count is programmatically associated with the results list so it is announced to screen readers (e.g. an aria-live='polite' region announcing e.g. "12 stays match your search") and updates without moving keyboard focus or forcing a re-focus of the results container.
- The count is reachable/settable only from the existing results markup and follows the app's existing UI conventions (same component style, spacing, and class naming as the current search results header), keeping the diff small.
- Focused automated coverage is added (unit/component tests) asserting the count text renders correctly for 0, 1, and N results and that it updates when filters or search change; an accessibility assertion verifies the live region announces the updated count and that focus is not moved on update.
- Existing search and filter behavior is unchanged: results still render and update exactly as before, independent of the pending reservation confirmation work.
